OPPS.title: Write thank-you cards for hospital staff
slots: Whenever you are free this week
OPPS.about: You get a printable card template. Write short notes to nurses and ward staff, then hand them in at your nearest drop box. Takes about 20 minutes.
rev: I did it between classes. Easy first step.
Simple, and the trust sent a thank-you note back.

OPPS.title: Evening reading hour with children
OPPS.about: Read aloud with a small group of children aged 6 to 9. A trained coordinator is in the room and gives you a story list before you start.
rev: I was nervous. The coordinator made it easy and the kids were great.
Went after work. One hour, and I felt useful.

OPPS.title: Teach phone basics to seniors
OPPS.about: Sit with two or three seniors and show them how to video-call family, pay with UPI and spot scam messages. A printed checklist keeps it simple.
rev: They were so patient with me too. Best Wednesday in months.

OPPS.title: Sort donated books for the street library
OPPS.about: Sort, label and shelve donated books by reading level. Most volunteers come in pairs, and it is quiet, satisfying work.
rev: Came with my sister. Chai, books and good music.

OPPS.title: Pack and hand out Saturday meals
OPPS.where: Kitchen on Station Road, 2.4 km away
OPPS.about: Pack meals in the morning and hand them out with a team lead on a fixed route. Gloves and aprons are provided.
rev: Well organised. We finished on time and got a proper debrief.

OPPS.title: Lake clean-up walk
OPPS.where: North gate of the lake, 2.8 km away
OPPS.about: Walk the lake path in small teams, pick up plastic and log what you find on a shared sheet. Breakfast at the gate after.
OPPS.fin: Spends shared in the group monthly
rev: Early start, but the sunrise on the lake was worth it.

OPPS.title: Plant saplings at the canal park
OPPS.about: Dig, plant and water 60 saplings with the ward group. A forester shows you how, and you can take a photo by your tree.
OPPS.fin: Spends shared in the group monthly

OPPS.title: Help Class 9 students with English, online
OPPS.about: Practise speaking with two students on a video call. You get a 15-minute guide first and a topic list for each session.
OPPS.bring: A phone or laptop with a camera
rev: Half an hour from my sofa. Surprisingly rewarding.

REQS.task: Read out my pharmacy bills and sort my tablets
REQS.note: My eyesight is weak. A short visit is enough.

REQS.task: Carry grocery bags up to the third floor
REQS.note: No lift in the building. Two bags, not heavy.

REQS.task: Explain two maths problems on a video call
REQS.note: Quadratic equations. A parent will be at home.

REQS.task: Set up UPI on my new phone
REQS.note: My son usually helps but he is travelling.

REQS.task: Feeding drive for street dogs needs 3 more helpers
REQS.note: We bring the food. You help serve and clean up.

GROUPS.name: 4th Block Reading Circle
GROUPS.about: Story hours and a street library

POSTS.text: 14 saplings planted at the canal park on Sunday. Thank you to the 19 of you who came. Next planting is in two weeks.
Dog feeding this Sunday needs 3 more people. 45 minutes, and the food is covered.
The street library crossed 600 books this month. Pustak Ghar needs sorters on Saturday afternoon.

HISTORY.title: Pack and hand out Saturday meals

TIPS: Meet in a public or shared space, or bring a friend
Chat in the app. Your number stays private
Tell someone at home where you are going
Report anything that feels off with one tap

REFS.take: One tap connects a person who needs help with a person who can give it. Our “I can help” button works the same way.
A calm live map where urgency shows through pulsing pins. Today’s requests pulse on our Help map.
Large type and language switching always within reach. Hindi is one tap from every home screen.
Dimensional icons that react when pressed, a 2×2 fact grid on listings, and a split list and map on desktop.

REFS.aw: Named by Apple among the best apps (2023)
REFS.take: Time windows and spots left lead every card. Ours lead with minutes, not causes.

REFS.aw: Design Museum, Beazley Designs of the Year 2019
REFS.take: Neighbour-to-neighbour posts in two fields, sorted by distance. Our Ask for help form copies that lightness.
A bold split hero and a focused five-section navigation. Our desktop rail has five destinations.
Filter by theme without leaving the page. Our cause and time filters update the list and map together.

REFS.aw: Webby nominee, City and Urban Innovation
REFS.take: Short, one-off roles that fit around life. Our 20-minute first step comes from the same insight.
A local interactive map makes the cause personal. Ours centres on you and your 3 km.

welcome: 65% of India’s volunteers gave five hours or less in a month, so we ask about time and default to short starts.
Your answers set the home screen: the time filter and which path opens first.
home: 88% of volunteering in India is informal, so Help nearby sits beside Join an activity instead of hiding in a menu.
Time chips answer the top enabler after money: flexible schedules (25.5%).
The dark card is a 20-minute task you can do from home. It is the smallest way in.
help: 81% of volunteering is self-organised. Requests from verified neighbours are sorted by distance.
Today’s requests pulse on the map so the urgent ones stand out.
Start a drive and Ask for help are one tap away.
detail: Verified host and published finances come first. Newcomers find credible groups hard to spot.
The 2×2 grid shows when, how long, where and spots left at a glance.
One tap shares to WhatsApp. Seniors rely on word of mouth (92%), students on social (52%).
success: Close the loop from day one
Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of a first-timer returning, so we confirm, remind and invite a friend straight away.
A reminder and a calendar add reduce no-shows.
request: Informal help, with safety built in
The exact address is shared only after you accept. Chat stays in the app.
Badges show how each person was checked.
Safety tips appear before you commit, not buried in settings.
chat: Most informal help is a short, one-off favour. Preset replies make coordination fast, also in Hindi.
drive: Starting a drive takes three steps and ends in a WhatsApp invite, where people already organise.
Hosts need a verified phone. ID verification unlocks larger drives.
ask: People who avoid organisations still need and give help. A two-field request keeps it light.
community: Peer influence keeps people coming back
Social norms predict retention at every stage. Groups show what neighbours did and invite you to the next one.
activity: Past activities ask one question and offer a next step in one tap.
feedback: One question, then a next step
Three faces, no forms. A good experience leads straight to the next session.
me: Students get hours and certificates. Everyone can hide them: homemakers and seniors told researchers they do not want badges.
